rounds.text: Tera Software Ltd is dramatically under-appreciated by the market, as evidenced by a discounted cash flow valuation pointing to an intrinsic value of Rs 815 per share against a market price of ₹ 380, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 53.4% [E44, E45]. The company's recent operational performance is exceptionally strong, marked by compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months of 121% and compounded profit growth of 162% over the same period [E17, E21]. This massive acceleration in fundamentals is underscored by an operating margin that surged to 15% in Mar 2026 from -8% three years earlier, representing a dramatic 23 percentage point expansion [E30]. Furthermore, the business commands a robust ROCE of 24.4% and an ROE of 18.5%, significantly outperforming the broader sector median ROCE of 12.2% [E12, E13, E75]. The company benefits directly from a supportive Information Technology sector tailwind score of +0.64, while a rules-based screen scores the setup at 77 out of 100 with a medium confidence BUY rating [E63, E72]. Conceded: [E34], [E36], [E62].

Despite recent headline profit growth, Tera Software Ltd carries severe underlying cash generation and working capital risks that undermine the reported earnings quality [E34]. Operating cash flow turned aggressively negative to Rs -14 Cr in Mar 2026, meaning cash conversion collapsed to -0.56x against reported profit, while free cash flow deteriorated further to Rs -16 Cr [E34, E35, E36]. This cash drain coincides with a dangerous bloating of working capital tied to exceptionally high debtors averaging 243 days [E62]. To fund this shortfall, borrowings surged nearly 100% in a single year from Rs 20 Cr to Rs 39 Cr as of Mar 2026 [E39]. Compounding these operational headwinds, historical performance reveals a weak long-term core, marked by a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of just 3% and a paltry 10-year median return on equity of 4% [E14, E26]. Furthermore, technical momentum is entirely absent, with the stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside a punishing historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -89.9% [E49, E52]. conceded: [E44]

While the bear highlights a negative operating cash flow of Rs -14 Cr in Mar 2026, this cash pressure is heavily offset by a healthy debt-to-equity ratio of 0.27x and a conservative capital structure [E35, E38]. The long-term historical sales growth of 3% over ten years is superseded by explosive near-term acceleration, featuring a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 121% and a 3-year compounded rate of 22% [E14, E16, E17]. Conceded: [E62]. Although historical 10-year median ROE was low at 4%, recent profitability has expanded dramatically, with return on equity reaching 18% over the last year alongside a strong ROCE of 24.4% [E26, E12, E29]. The operating margin trajectory demonstrates substantial structural improvement, expanding by 23 percentage points over three years to 15% in Mar 2026 with an increasing multi-year trend [E30, E32].

Conceded: [E35, E38]. While the bull points to a conservative capital structure to excuse the negative cash position, borrowings actually jumped significantly from Rs 20 Cr to Rs 39 Cr in Mar 2026 while generating a negative operating cash flow of Rs -14 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -16 Cr [E35, E36, E39]. Conceded: [E14, E16, E17]. However, looking at the long-term track record reveals a cyclical or stagnant core, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of just 3% and a 10-year median ROE of a meager 4% [E14, E26]. Conceded: [E12, E29, E30, E32]. Despite these recent margin expansions and higher returns, the company suffers from severely bloated working capital represented by high debtors of 243 days, explaining why reported profits fail to materialize into actual cash [E34, E62]. Furthermore, the technical and structural momentum is deteriorating, with the stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -89.9% and high annualised volatility of 67.4% [E49, E52, E53].
